items.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, I think I would drag you, what other jobs have you done? Slater, different things you used to tell me, what other jobs? [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, yeah, I used to work, first I used to work for Al Mastricht... and I used to do all the slater work...

ctx.x: Well, let me see what you had done. That wasn't so long ago. You see, 19, that's before in New York, no, after we come from New York. 1847, I think. I think it was, yeah, 1947, yeah, I think it was 1947. And I come in, and the North Shore showed me a place where I couldn't fix that place. And we had to play the St. Joseph Knight. And it was about five days or six days for the St. Joseph Knight. So you need iron clamp. I said, I don't need iron clamp, I know what to do then. I took my wood, make my iron clamp on…
Well, I think I would drag you, what other jobs have you done? Slater, different things you used to tell me, what other jobs?

Oh, yeah, I used to work, first I used to work for Al Mastricht, 919 on Lobster Street, and I used to do all the slater work, paper hanging, plaster, that's my tray, and I knew that I'd do carbonate work. And I done all that. I went for D'Alandino real estate at 729 Newton Street. I done all that for D'Alandino real estate. And now I went for Miss Ducco at 1301 Barrett Street. She's dead, and her sister died, and all of them cats are from Miss Ducco. My father and neighbors, my parents used to be at a bigger…
